events.text:
🇦🇪 UAE control of Red Sea's geostrategic jewel Berbera signals expansion of Iran war
The UAE’s control over Somaliland’s Berbera port is where its commercial interests and military strategy overlap.
The firm DP World, then headed by Epstein pen pal Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem, signed a 30-year deal in May 2016 to operate the deep-water port of Berbera that was worth $442 million.
In 2017, Somaliland’s parliament approved the establishment of an Emirati military base in Berbera, granting the UAE access to the Soviet-era 4,140-meter runway and other air facilities.
Berbera’s strategic significance
The deep-water gateway on the Gulf of Aden is strategically close — just 300 km — to the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait. This allows the UAE to project naval and air power across the waterway and challenge both Yemen's Ansar Allah and Saudi interests in the region.
The military base is being expanded for potential future joint use by the UAE, Israel and the US, Le Monde reported in July, [citing satellite imagery](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72671). OSINT accounts on X suggest the construction of new SAM sites, radar positions, UAV and aircraft hangars, as well as multiple underground structures, bunkers and ammunition storage facilities.
Berbera’s commercial role is also growing as businesses increasingly shift toward the Red Sea amid the Strait of Hormuz crisis.
Somaliland: An arena for a new geostrategic battle?
During his recent visit to the US, Somaliland leader Cabdiraxmaan Cirro promoted his country and Berbera port as a strategic Red Sea gateway for the US and a potential foothold [against the Houthis](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74720). Military experts warn that the ongoing Middle East conflict could spill over into Somaliland and the broader African region.
